_doc: TEMPLATE for exercise_codegen.py copy this file to define a new exercise.
Usage:  python3 tools/dev/exercise_codegen.py tools/dev/exercises/my_exercise.json
Add --dry-run to preview the generated Scala without writing to the registry.
FIELD REFERENCE
scalaName    – Scala val identifier, lowerCamelCase, e.g. 'myExercise'
The codegen derives 'myExerciseExerciseId' from this automatically.
exerciseId   – Stable string key used in persistence and routing.
Prefix convention:  block:  for function exercises,
script: for top-level script exercises.
NEVER rename an existing id once it is in production.
title        – Short display name shown in the UI.  Required: en, de.
statement    – Full exercise description shown to the student.
Backticks for inline code are supported: `my_func(x)`.
Newlines can be encoded as \n for multi-paragraph statements.
Required: en, de.
config flags (all boolean, default true if omitted):
enableVmStaticChecks      – run the VM-level static analysis pass
enablePythonStaticChecks  – run pyodide-level static analysis
enableUnitTests           – run the visible + hidden test suite
enableAiSummary           – include an LLM-generated summary in feedback
timeoutMs    – Python execution timeout in milliseconds (default 4000).
Increase for exercises that need sorting / heavy computation.
visibleTests / hiddenTests – arrays of test objects (see below).
fixtures     – list of setup code strings prepended before every test.
Use for helper functions or shared state.  Usually [].
packages     – list of pip package names to install before running (pyodide).
Usually [].  Example: ["numpy"].
TEST OBJECT FIELDS
name    (required) – snake_case identifier, unique within the exercise.
code    (required) – one-line assert statement executed as a Python test.
weight  (optional) – scoring multiplier for this test, default 1.0.
Use 2.0 for edge-case / harder tests.
hint    (optional) – English hint shown when this specific test fails.
hintDE  (optional) – German translation of the hint.
NAMING CONVENTIONS
visible tests  – cover the happy path the student sees in the problem statement.
hidden tests   – cover edge cases, corner values, large inputs, negative numbers.
ESCAPE SEQUENCES IN test.code
Store them as JSON escape sequences, NOT as actual characters.
Example: a literal backslash-t in the Python string → write \\t in JSON.
The codegen re-escapes correctly for the Scala string literal layer.

visibleTests._note: Happy-path test — no hint needed when the case is obvious.
visibleTests.name: basic_case

visibleTests._note: Second visible test with bilingual hints.
visibleTests.name: another_case
visibleTests.hint: Consider what happens when the input is zero.
visibleTests.hintDE: Überlege, was passiert, wenn die Eingabe null ist.

hiddenTests._note: Edge case — default weight 1.0, no hint required.
hiddenTests.name: negative_input

hiddenTests._note: Harder edge case — higher weight and bilingual hints.
hiddenTests.name: large_value
hiddenTests.hint: Make sure your solution handles large inputs efficiently.
hiddenTests.hintDE: Stelle sicher, dass deine Lösung große Eingaben effizient verarbeitet.
